editorialRead.readHeadline: NousResearch/hermes-agent is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: NousResearch/hermes-agent leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 27 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 27 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: NousResearch/hermes-agent — 178 commits today, 54.7 below its current daily pace, with 175 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
openclaw/openclaw — 40 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
anomalyco/opencode — No same-day commit after 93 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Watch whether every delegated Hermes task now receives the repository’s working rules
dailyInsight.insight: Hermes Agent has moved workspace context from a review-specific path into its shared child-prompt builder. Teams that depend on repository instructions should watch one harmless delegated task: does the child receive the same project conventions as its parent, while an empty or ambiguous workspace stays empty rather than inheriting a guessed directory?
dailyInsight.mechanism: The fresh public commit routes the parent’s resolved workspace path through `build_context_files_prompt` for every `delegate_task` child, including reviewers. It uses the existing priority order for `.hermes.md`, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and `.cursorrules`, deliberately skips SOUL.md, removes a review-local duplicate loader, and adds real-filesystem, empty-workspace, and reviewer end-to-end tests.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: Delegation is a behavioral boundary: a parent can follow a repository’s conventions while a child silently works without them. The suggested check is limited and reversible. It is not a claim that the commit has shipped in a release, that every external agent follows the same convention, or that a context file makes a delegated action safe.

actions.audience: Maintainer or operator of a Hermes Agent workflow that delegates review or implementation work inside repositories with project instructions
actions.label: Observe one harmless child task at the context boundary
actions.instruction: In a disposable repository, place one non-sensitive, testable instruction in the project’s normal context-file chain. Ask a parent task to delegate a harmless check that requires that instruction, then repeat in an empty or explicitly unrelated workspace. Record whether the child follows the project rule only in the resolved workspace; do not use the result to infer access, authorization, or release availability.

receipts.title: feat: every subagent's prompt embeds the workspace's project context files
receipts.supports: Shows the public merged change, its explicit context-file order, its use for all delegate_task children, and the stated refusal to infer a bare current working directory.

receipts.title: Child-prompt construction and delegation implementation at commit 7526bd39a8
receipts.supports: Shows the child-prompt path that receives the resolved workspace context and the implementation location named by the commit.

confidence.basis: The fresh public commit and inspected delegation implementation agree that the change broadens repository-context loading to delegated children. The call remains a watch because the sources are main-branch implementation and tests, not a released or independently reproduced workflow.

dailyInsight.limitation: The receipts do not establish release availability, the behavior of a particular deployed Hermes installation, whether every supported context file is safe to inject into every task, or whether a child will correctly apply a rule once it receives it.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise or withdraw the call if a public regression shows a delegated child omitting a resolved project context, loading context from an unrelated or bare working directory, or a release note narrows the feature away from ordinary delegate_task children.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for a released integration test that demonstrates parent and child behavior across a real repository, a no-workspace invocation, and a reviewer task without exposing sensitive project instructions.
